questions.stem: What is the size range of nanoparticles?
questions.explanation: Nanoparticles are particles between 1 nm and 100 nm in diameter. This is much smaller than fine particles (100-2500 nm) and bulk materials (greater than 1 mm). A nanoparticle typically contains a few hundred to a few thousand atoms.

questions.stem: Why are nanoparticles more reactive than bulk materials of the same substance?

options.text: Nanoparticles are made of different atoms than bulk materials
Nanoparticles have a much higher surface area to volume ratio, so more atoms are exposed to react
Nanoparticles contain more energy than bulk materials
Nanoparticles have stronger bonds that release more energy

questions.explanation: As particles get smaller, their surface area to volume ratio increases dramatically. This means a much greater proportion of atoms are on the surface and available to take part in reactions. Since chemical reactions happen at surfaces, nanoparticles are significantly more reactive than the same mass of bulk material.
